notes: The example-health-apis error writer HCAZERRS, run as a started task: ASSIGN SYSID / STARTCODE / PRINSYSID / INVOKINGPROG, then, with no invoking program, RECEIVE INTO the 79-byte WS-RECV, WRITEQ TD to CSMT and WRITEQ TS to HCAZERRS (LENGTH = received length, the region SYSID in front of the text), SEND TEXT and RETURN. The harness names no invoking program, so the program's other arm (INVOKINGPROG not blank: the caller's COMMAREA is the message, no SEND TEXT) is not reachable from a case: the same open pair as genapp-lgstsq's LGSTSQ (68:true, 113:false there). The task's STARTCODE is stated as TD (a terminal-started transaction): ASSIGN STARTCODE is a fact of the run the equivalence harness refuses unless a case states it (oracle_assumptions.md X19). The region SYSID is a deployment fact the corpus does not name. Derived from IBM's example-health-apis (github.com/ibm/example-health-apis, Apache-2.0; (C) Copyright IBM Corp. 2011, 2014): LICENSE here is the corpus's own, NOTICE names the source and what was derived.

region.why: a deployment fact: HCAZERRS ASSIGNs SYSID into the message it writes; the corpus names no region

scenarios.name: caller-error-record
scenarios.why: the shape the estate's callers write (date, time, program, key, SQLCODE) after the 5-byte transid

scenarios.name: full-width-message
scenarios.why: the longest message WS-RECV holds: transid plus 74 data bytes

scenarios.name: short-message
scenarios.why: a short message: only the received length is logged

scenarios.name: transid-only
scenarios.why: the transid alone: received length 4 under the 5 the program subtracts, then adds back

scenarios.name: transid-and-blank
scenarios.why: the transid and the separating blank: no message text

scenarios.name: message-past-79
scenarios.why: input longer than WS-RECV: the RECEIVE LENGTH(80) truncates it (the oracle's judgement of the overlong receive)
